executiveSummary: Arkansas maintains a state-controlled County Voting System Grant Fund (CVSGF) fed largely by UCC filing fees remitted by the Secretary of State, plus periodic legislative appropriations and a one-time 2019 Property Tax Relief transfer. The SOS establishes grant guidelines under A.C.A. § 7-5-301. FY2025–26 appropriates $11M from CVSGF and $4M federal HAVA. No consolidated public county-by-county award dashboard has been located — but county budgets and SOS historical records confirm disbursements occurred. Kelly's frame: election transparency includes funding transparency; SOS must publish equitable, readable grant accounting.

recordsRequest.title: Targeted administrative records request — not a broad FOIA fishing expedition
recordsRequest.exactAsk: Please provide county-by-county distribution records for the County Voting System Grant Fund from FY2018 through FY2027, including: county name, award amount, award date, purpose, equipment/vendor where applicable, and fund source (state CVSGF vs federal HAVA vs other).
alsoRequest: Reimbursement ledgers and equipment transfer records
Grant application approvals and denials by county
Any existing statewide summary report not published online
recordsRequest.framing: Legitimate for a Secretary of State candidate studying election administration — normal policy research, not accusatory.

sosOutreach.recommendedContact: Arkansas Secretary of State Elections Division — verify current staff (research suggested Leslie Oguinn as operational contact)
sosOutreach.approach: Serious policy learner — not opponent trying to catch them
sosOutreach.openingScript: I'm trying to better understand how election administration funding flows through Arkansas — both federal HAVA funding and the County Voting System Grant Fund. I'm particularly interested in how county support decisions are made and whether there are county-by-county public reports available.
questionsToAsk: Is there a statewide county distribution spreadsheet available to the public?
Are grants reimbursement-based, allocated, or direct equipment purchase?
How are priorities determined across rural and urban counties?
What responsibilities sit with SOS vs counties vs State Board of Election Commissioners?
What major unmet county needs still exist?
How do UCC fee collections track to CVSGF balances year over year?
doNotOpenWith: Why are you hiding county grants?
sosOutreach.strategicGoal: Become known as the candidate who understands election administration — not just election politics

debateStrategy.kellyFrame: Arkansas has real state election equipment funding — UCC fees and legislative appropriations flow through a SOS-controlled grant fund. Integrity includes funding transparency: clerks and voters deserve a public county-by-county accounting, not just appropriations headlines.
debateStrategy.hammerLikelyFrame: I secured funding for voting equipment / Arkansas elections are #1 / I wrote the integrity laws.
debateStrategy.hammerTrapQuestion: Senator, you cite integrity packages — can you point to the county-by-county grant ledger showing which counties received CVSGF dollars after each mandate you sponsored?
debateStrategy.hammerRebuttalIfHeCounters: If he cites Act 808 or appropriations totals: 'Totals in Little Rock are not the same as implementation in every county — show the ledger.' If he cites #1 ranking: 'Ranking is not a substitute for clerk training dollars — SOS grant guidelines are your job to publish.'
debateStrategy.packoAngle: May agree funding is opaque — Kelly adds operational SOS plan without attacking Pakko.
doNotSay: They are hiding money (accusatory without ledger proof)
Counties got nothing (contradicted by budget breadcrumbs and Act 808)
Precise FY2026-27 figures until enrolled act verified
debateStrategy.fairPublicLine: I've been researching how election funding flows to Arkansas counties, and it is surprisingly difficult for the public to find a clear county-by-county accounting — election transparency should include election funding transparency.

verifiedClaimsForLedger.sourceHint: A.C.A. § 19-5-1247; SOS UCC fee page; IRG white paper

verifiedClaimsForLedger.claimText: The Secretary of State establishes guidelines and procedures for distributing CVSGF grants to counties (A.C.A. § 7-5-301(d)(2)).
Act 408 of 2025 (HB1147) appropriated $11,000,000 from the County Voting System Grant Fund to the SOS for FY2025-2026.
Act 408 of 2025 appropriated $4,000,000 in federal Help America Vote Act funds to the SOS for FY2025-2026.
Act 808 of 2019 transferred $8.24 million from the Property Tax Relief Fund to the County Voting System Grant Fund for county voting equipment.
No consolidated public statewide county-by-county CVSGF award table has been located in open research.
Garland County budget records document a $14,340 Secretary of State Voting System Grant appropriation (2015).
